title: How many rows does the query touch?
predict: The table has 10,000 users. How many rows does each query read?
caption: Hashing in the WHERE clause makes the database hash every email to find the match, on every request. A stored, indexed hash is one lookup. Not storing a derivable value cost a full scan, so store it.

title: The old face, and how long it lingers
predict: User 1 changes their photo. With a two-day TTL and no invalidation, how long might user 2 see the old face?
caption: With only a 1–2 day TTL, the CDN can keep serving the old photo until it expires. An event on Kafka lets a worker call the CDN's purge API (or the API calls it directly), and the next request gets the new photo. Long TTL for speed, explicit invalidation for correctness.

title: Three people, not three hundred messages
predict: 300 messages from 3 friends arrive while you're offline. What does the badge show, and what does one tap change?
caption: In this design the badge counts unique senders since your last tap: 300 messages from three people show 3. A tap clears the set and the badge, but nothing was read.

title: Thirty messages, one write
predict: C sends 30 messages. How many reach the main Redis, with and without the auxiliary?
caption: Without help, all 30 writes hit the main store and 29 change nothing. With an auxiliary store, the repeats stop at a cheap existence check and the main store gets one write per sender. Shield the brittle database from work that changes nothing.
